dossier.architecture: Second complete robot adds full-width coral ground pickup to elevator/arm architecture.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module variant unresolved here.
subsystems.intake: Rebuild collector uses lightweight hollow rollers, compliant star wheels and floating front; original robot lacked this full-width intake.
subsystems.transfer: Polycarbonate funnel and three location sensors coordinate automatic handoff to claw.
subsystems.scoring: Two-stage internally belted elevator; independently tensioned up/down runs, large arm bearings and carbon tube. Shared pinch claw handles both pieces.
subsystems.endgame: Powered cage capture; over-center four-bar stops cage impact from bouncing mechanism away. Earlier robot combined algae/climb functions according to separate contemporary discussion, not fully audited here.
subsystems.controls: Single controller, state-machine handoff, profiled alignment and driver scoring confirmation.

versions: Worlds interview explicitly concerns the season's second robot.
Rebuild changed collection and endgame architecture; original full subsystem documentation remains incomplete.
dossier.analysis: A rebuild can be justified by a missing acquisition capability rather than insufficient scoring reach. The intake was the team's highest-risk unresolved prototype; copying the finished elevator would not have resolved that risk.

context_documents.title: 2025-4414 · The rebuild’s full-width intake changes the robot’s supply model
context_documents.body:
# 2025-4414: The rebuild’s full-width intake changes the robot’s supply model

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview explicitly identifies this as the second robot and says the original lacked the rebuild’s full-width ground collector. Hollow rollers, compliant star wheels and a floating front feed a polycarbonate funnel and sensor-guided handoff. A continuous internally belted elevator and carbon-tube arm carry a shared pinch claw for coral/algae.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links hollow rollers to weight reduction and identifies the wide ground collector as a major rebuild objective. It reports testing the star-wheel contact choice rather than presenting it as an arbitrary styling decision.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The historical lineage should be specific: the team mentions 254’s 2022 hollow-roller construction, while the 2025 task requires orienting rigid coral rather than simply transporting foam cargo. Copying fabrication technique is different from copying an entire intake path. A shared pinch claw can reduce moving mechanisms but its force and retained orientation must remain acceptable for two very different pieces.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test pickup orientation tolerance, failed handoff recovery, and claw retention through rapid arm motion. Keep the original and rebuild capabilities separate in recommendations and comparisons.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: HighTide Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.locator: April 23 description and older corpus supplement
source_reviews.review_basis: Read publisher description and older synopsis separately. Full captions not retrieved.
facts: Publisher identifies the filmed robot as rebuilt and highlights ground intake, dual-purpose claw and climb. Retained synopsis describes internal belt tensioning, three transfer sensors and over-center cage linkage.
source_reviews.limitations: The description supports the broad architecture. Detailed mechanics are inherited.

source_reviews.title: HighTide OVERHEAD reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team reveal text and discussion.
facts: The initial reveal was named OVERHEAD. The team qualified it as its robot at the time.
source_reviews.limitations: Jokes and viewer comments do not establish the actual intake or climber configuration.

source_reviews.title: FIRST 2025 Team 4414
source_reviews.limitations: Listing does not give a version timeline.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The useful contrast is between the early OVERHEAD reveal and the rebuilt robot at Worlds. The rebuilt machine combines floor pickup, an elevator and a claw shared by both pieces. The key design burden is the handoff: pipes presented with varying pose must reach the claw at a repeatable height and alignment before the arm can move. A separate powered cage capture then needs to survive a collision with the hanging target without occupying that same deployed envelope.
piece_flow: Floor coral enters a wide floating roller arrangement in the retained account, travels through a polycarbonate funnel and reaches the claw.
Elevator and arm move the shared claw to the reef. The claw also handles algae on its own cycle.
The retained controls synopsis describes automated transfer and driver confirmation for placement.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The rebuild places the floor collector, funnel, two-stage lift and claw along a common piece route. Large pivot bearings and a carbon arm tube are retained details. Independently tensioned belt runs could simplify tuning, but any asymmetry or guide play can appear as error at the claw. Analyze the climb linkage swept envelope alongside the stowed collector.

subsystems.name: Ground intake and transfer
subsystems.construction: Full-width floating front, hollow rollers and compliant star wheels per older dossier.
subsystems.operation: Collect coral and constrain the piece through the funnel. Three location sensors coordinate the handoff in the retained account.
subsystems.team_rationale: The retained study identifies acquisition capability as a rebuild driver.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Collector width is valuable only where the accepted pipe poses converge to the claw throat. The outer pickup lanes can be harder to center than the middle.
subsystems.interfaces: Floor, bumper lip, funnel and elevator load height form a series of narrow interfaces.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test bent side plate, a stalled funnel pipe and a sensor stuck true. Measure access to each roller and sensor.
subsystems.unknowns: Handoff timing, sensor geometry and original-robot intake details.

subsystems.name: Elevator, arm and claw
subsystems.construction: Two-stage internal belts, separately tensionable runs and carbon-tube arm are inherited construction details.
subsystems.operation: Raise the shared pinch claw and orient either coral or algae. Coordinate motion with chassis alignment.
subsystems.team_rationale: Publisher confirms dual-purpose claw. Fine-grained choices remain sourced to prior notes.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A single claw reduces the need for dedicated travel paths while requiring adequate compression and clear exit geometry for two unlike pieces.
subsystems.interfaces: Check claw release under elevator racking and under actual reef interference.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure stage play and arm tip error at high extension after impact. Verify that a lost piece can be cleared without lifting into the reef.
subsystems.unknowns: Belt routing, arm ratios, and as-built tolerances.

subsystems.name: Cage capture
subsystems.construction: Powered grab and over-center four-bar per retained synopsis.
subsystems.operation: Present capture mechanism to the cage and hold geometry through approach impact.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older synopsis links over-center geometry to resisting bounce away.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Over-center margin is sensitive to slop and deformation. Cage impact direction and actual stop contact should be part of the validation.
subsystems.interfaces: The intake and claw must clear approach and hang poses.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test from both yaw directions and inspect the hard stop after a miss.

revisions: February OVERHEAD reveal and April rebuilt robot are documented separately. Specific funnel, belt and cage changes beyond that comparison remain inherited.
transferable_principles: Prototype the widest intended floor intake and actual handoff together.
Budget clearances at every linkage transition, including impact.
disconfirming_conditions: Reliable station supply can reduce the value of a wholesale floor acquisition rebuild.
A more flexible or worn four-bar can lose its intended over-center margin.
remaining_gaps: Full captions, primary technical text for the rebuild and installation chronology.

recommended_images.locator: Candidate frames of collector-to-claw path, elevator belt tensioners and four-bar cage approach
